outcome: A preprint by Gong, Wu, Xie and Yu (arXiv:2310.01219, latest revision Feb 2025) proves the rational strong Novikov conjecture for countable discrete subgroups of the full diffeomorphism group of a compact smooth manifold, removing the volume-preserving hypothesis required by the authors' own 2018/2021 result (arXiv:1811.02086, published in GAFA 2021). This settles a new case of the fundamental-group classes for which the Novikov conjecture is known, but the paper remains an unpublished, unreviewed preprint and the general conjecture is untouched.
summary: The triage flagged arXiv:2310.01219 (Gong, Wu, Xie, Yu), which proves the rational strong Novikov conjecture for countable discrete subgroups of the diffeomorphism group Diff(M) of a compact smooth manifold M, removing the volume-preserving restriction that the same authors' earlier paper (arXiv:1811.02086, published in Geometric and Functional Analysis in 2021) had required. I read the arXiv abstract/metadata directly rather than relying on the triage note. This is a genuine case of the Novikov conjecture under §3.1: it restricts the stated fundamental-group question (which groups can arise as π1 of a manifold for which the conjecture is verified) and settles a strictly larger class than was previously known, so it removes territory from the open problem rather than merely restating it under different hypotheses. However: (1) the initial submission was 2023-10-02, before the 26 Jan 2024 frozen-revision date; only the v2 (Aug 2024) and v3 (Feb 2025) revisions fall inside the window, and I found no indication the mathematical content of the diffeomorphism-group result itself was new to v2/v3 rather than already present in v1 — the paper's core claim (proving the conjecture for the full diffeomorphism group, not just volume-preserving) was already in the October 2023 v1 based on the abstract's framing. Given the ambiguity about what changed between versions, and following the instruction to date by the first public written argument, I dated the event to the original 2023-10-02 submission, which makes it fall outside the window (predates_frozen_revision: true). No later independent event within the window resolves a further case: I found no other paper, announcement, or digestion of this preprint between 26 Jan 2024 and now. The paper is still unpublished (no journal reference in its arXiv metadata, comments field just says '103 pages, comments are welcome') and I found no expert digestion (blog, survey, or journal acceptance) of it. On strict application of §6.3 ('date the first public written argument'), this event is open_stale-adjacent, but because I cannot confirm the diffeomorphism-group generalization was fully present and unchanged in v1 versus being substantively expanded/corrected in the Aug 2024 or Feb 2025 revisions (which do fall in the window), I record status as partial with the date at first submission and flag this dating uncertainty explicitly rather than silently classifying it as open_stale. No AI system is mentioned anywhere in the paper's abstract, metadata, or in any secondary source I found discussing it — the work uses operator K-theory, Hilbert-Hadamard spaces, and classical geometric group theory. I also searched broadly for any AI-related activity on the Novikov conjecture generally (proofs, counterexamples, bound improvements, or incidents) and found none; general AI-in-mathematics roundups (IMO 2024 AlphaProof/AlphaGeometry, various 2025-2026 'AI mathematician' pieces) do not mention the Novikov conjecture at all.
competing_reading: If the diffeomorphism-group (non-volume-preserving) generalization was only fully established in the Aug 2024 or Feb 2025 revision — i.e., v1 (Oct 2023) proved a weaker or different statement that was strengthened inside the window — then the correct event date is 2024-08 or 2025-02, both inside the window, and predates_frozen_revision should be false with no open_stale concern. The abstract text available to me describes the final (v3) claim and does not clearly state what v1 claimed differently. It is also possible a careful reading would treat this as open_stale (event predates window, no in-window event), since I found no evidence of an in-window development beyond arXiv revision timestamps of the same paper.
what_would_settle_it: Diffing v1 (Oct 2023) against v3 (Feb 2025) of arXiv:2310.01219 to see whether the core theorem (Novikov conjecture for discrete, non-volume-preserving Diff(M) subgroups) was present in v1 or only added/strengthened in a later revision, and checking whether any journal has since accepted the paper or any expert (e.g. a survey, ICM report, or blog by a specialist in coarse geometry/K-theory) has digested it.
